def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-vel:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set, where Lipschitz means that $\partial D$ has a finite rigidly moved graph-chart atlas. Here $H^1_0(D)$ is the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(D)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Since $D$ has finite measure, Holder makes every $L^2$ class integrable, so the zero-mean condition is well-defined ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]). Define
$$V:=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d),\qquad Q:=L^2_0(D):=\{q\in L^2(D;\mathbb R):\int_Dq=0\}.$$
Equip $V$ with $\|v\|_V:=\|
abla v\|_{L^2(D)}$ and $Q$ with $\|q\|_Q:=\|q\|_{L^2(D)}$. The local Poincare inequality [[lem-na-homogeneous-dirichlet-poincare]] makes the first a norm equivalent to the usual $H^1$ norm. For $v\in V$, define $\varepsilon(v):=(
abla v+
abla v^T)/2$ and $b(v,q):=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$. For viscosity $
u>0$, set $a_
u(u,v):=2
u\int_D\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)$, where $X:Y=\sum_{i,j}X_{ij}Y_{ij}$. The continuous domain class is all bounded connected Lipschitz $D$; the exact mini-element mesh class is the narrower polygonal/polyhedral conforming affine simplicial class.
lem-na-zero-mean-of-zero-boundary-diverg:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open. If $v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, then $\operatorname{div}v\in L^2(D)$ and $\int_D\operatorname{div}v=0$.
lem-na-homogeneous-dirichlet-poincare:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, and suppose its first coordinate projection is contained in an interval $(a,b)$ of width $L=b-a$. For every real $v\in H^1_0(D)$,
$$\|v\|_{L^2(D)}\le L\|\partial_1v\|_{L^2(D)}\le L\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}.$$
lem-na-homogeneous-dirichlet-korn-identi:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For bounded open $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, put $\varepsilon(v)=(\nabla v+\nabla v^T)/2$. Then
$$2\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2^2=\|\nabla v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2,$$
so $\|\nabla v\|_2\le\sqrt2\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2$.
lem-na-lipschitz-domain-finite-star-shap:
## Statement

Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected and Lipschitz. Here Lipschitz means that its compact boundary has a finite atlas of rigidly moved cylinders in which $D$ is the strict epigraph $x_d>\varphi(x')$ of a Lipschitz function. There are finitely many bounded open sets $U_i\subset D$ covering $D$, each star-shaped with respect to a closed ball $\overline B_i\subset U_i$, and the graph joining $i,j$ when $U_i\cap U_j\ne\varnothing$ is connected. There are measurable sets $E_i\subset U_i$ partitioning $D$ and, for every edge of a spanning tree of this graph, a function $\psi_{ij}\in C_c^\infty(U_i\cap U_j)$ with integral one.
lem-na-finite-cover-zero-mean-data-decom:
## Statement

Let $D=\bigcup_{i=1}^N U_i$ be the finite connected star-shaped cover from [[lem-na-lipschitz-domain-finite-star-shaped-cover]], with measurable partition $E_i$ and normalized tree-edge bumps $\psi_e$. For every $q\in L^2_0(D)$ there are $q_i\in L^2_0(U_i)$, depending linearly on $q$, whose zero extensions satisfy $q=\sum_iq_i$ and
$$\|q_i\|_{L^2(U_i)}\le D_i\|q\|_{L^2(D)},\qquad D_i=1+|D|^{1/2}\sum_{e\text{ incident to }i}\|\psi_e\|_2.$$
def-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-integral:
## Definition

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, star-shaped with respect to a closed ball $\overline B(a,\rho)\subset U$. Choose $\omega\in C_c^\infty(B(a,\rho))$ with $\int\omega=1$. For $f\in C_c^\infty(U)$, initially define the vector-valued integral
$$ (\mathcal B_U f)(x)=\int_U f(y)(x-y)\int_0^1\omega\!\left(y+\frac{x-y}{t}\right)\frac{dt}{t^{d+1}}\,dy. $$
The inner integral is first interpreted for $t>0$; its locally integrable kernel, support and divergence identity are proved in the following lemma. All data and fields here are real. This definition makes no finite-quadrature or numerical-algorithm claim.
lem-na-bogovskii-kernel-support-and-dive:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U,\omega$ and $\mathcal B_U$ be as in [[def-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-integral]]. For $f\in C_c^\infty(U)$, write $G(x,y)=(x-y)\int_0^1\omega(y+(x-y)/t)t^{-d-1}dt$. Then $\mathcal B_Uf(x)=\int_UG(x,y)f(y)dy$ defines an $L^2$ field supported in a compact subset of $U$. Writing $K(x,y)=|G(x,y)|$ and $(\mathcal K_Ug)(x):=\int_UK(x,y)g(y)dy$, the majorant $\mathcal K_U|f|$ is also in $L^2(U)$, and $\mathcal K_U$ has a finite $L^2$ bound. Moreover,
$$\operatorname{div}\mathcal B_Uf=f-\omega\int_Uf$$
in distributions on $\mathbb R^d$. In particular, mean-zero input has divergence $f$.
lem-na-bogovskii-truncated-derivative-fo:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ and $\omega$ be as in [[def-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-integral]]. For $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ and $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$, use $\widehat g(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}g(x)dx$ and define
$$T_{\phi,j}^{\epsilon}f(x)=\int f(y)\int_\epsilon^1\partial_{x_j}\left[\phi\left(y+\frac{x-y}{t}\right)\right]\frac{dt}{t^d}dy.$$
As $\epsilon\downarrow0$ these converge in distributions to $T_{\phi,j}f$. The part with $0<t<1/2$ satisfies
$$\widehat{T^<_{\phi,j}f}(\xi)=2\pi i\xi_j\int_0^{1/2}\widehat\phi(t\xi)\widehat f((1-t)\xi)dt.$$
When $f\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the Bogovskii formula satisfies $\partial_j(\mathcal B_Uf)_k=T_{x_k\omega,j}f-T_{\omega,j}(y_kf)$ distributionally.
lem-na-bogovskii-fourier-ray-and-derivat:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ be bounded and open, $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$, and $\rho>0$. For every $\xi\in\mathbb R^d$ and coordinate $j$,
$$2\pi|\xi_j|\int_0^\infty|\widehat\phi(t\xi)|dt\le \rho^{-1}\|\phi\|_1+\rho\|\partial_j^2\phi\|_1.$$
If $T_{\phi,j}$ is the distributional operator of [[lem-na-bogovskii-truncated-derivative-fourier-formula]], then on functions supported in $U$,
$$\|T_{\phi,j}f\|_2\le A_j(\phi)\|f\|_2,\quad A_j(\phi)=2^{(d-1)/2}(\rho^{-1}\|\phi\|_1+\rho\|\partial_j^2\phi\|_1)+2^d|U|\|\partial_j\phi\|_\infty.$$
thm-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-bounded-rig:
## Statement

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, star-shaped with respect to a ball, and let $\omega$ and $\mathcal B_U$ be as in [[def-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-integral]]. Under Countable Choice there is a bounded linear extension $\mathcal B_U:L^2_0(U)\to H^1_0(U;\mathbb R^d)$ such that
$$\operatorname{div}\mathcal B_U f=f,\qquad \|\nabla\mathcal B_U f\|_2\le C_U\|f\|_2.$$
After translating the ball center to $0$, choose $R_U\ge\sup_{y\in U}|y|$ and define
$$A_j(\phi)=2^{(d-1)/2}\bigl(\rho^{-1}\|\phi\|_1+\rho\|\partial_j^2\phi\|_1\bigr)+2^d|U|\|\partial_j\phi\|_\infty.$$
One valid constant is $C_U=\left(\sum_{k,j=1}^d[A_j(x_k\omega)+R_UA_j(\omega)]^2\right)^{1/2}$.
thm-na-bounded-lipschitz-domain-divergen:
## Statement

Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected and Lipschitz, with $d\in\{2,3\}$. Under Countable Choice there is a bounded linear map $B_D:L^2_0(D)\to H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ such that
$$\operatorname{div}B_Dq=q,\qquad \|\nabla B_Dq\|_2\le C_{\rm div}(D)\|q\|_2.$$
For a chosen finite cover and tree decomposition from [[lem-na-lipschitz-domain-finite-star-shaped-cover]] and [[lem-na-finite-cover-zero-mean-data-decomposition]], one valid bound is $C_{\rm div}(D)=\sum_i C_{U_i}D_i$; it is finite and independent of any finite-element mesh.
thm-na-infsup-bounded-right-inverse-hilb:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V,Q$ be real Hilbert spaces and let $b:V\times Q\to\mathbb R$ be bounded. Define $B:V\to Q$ by $(Bv,q)_Q=b(v,q)$. If $Q=\{0\}$, the unique zero map is a bounded right inverse. If $Q\ne\{0\}$, assume $V\ne\{0\}$ and define
$$\beta:=\inf_{q\ne0}\sup_{v\ne0}\frac{b(v,q)}{\|v\|_V\|q\|_Q}.$$
When $\beta>0$, $B$ is onto and has a bounded linear right inverse $R:Q\to V$ with $BR=I_Q$ and $\|R\|\le\beta^{-1}$.
thm-na-continuous-stokes-divergence-infs:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. On the spaces $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$ of [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]], equipped with $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_2$, the form $b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$ is bounded by $\sqrt d$. Its inf-sup constant satisfies
$$\inf_{q\ne0}\sup_{v\ne0}\frac{b(v,q)}{\|v\|_V\|q\|_2}\ge C_{\rm div}(D)^{-1}.$$
def-na-fortin-operator:
## Definition

Let $V,Q,b$ be as in [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]], and let $V_h\subset V$, $Q_h\subset Q$ be finite-dimensional subspaces. A **Fortin operator** is a bounded linear map $\Pi_h:V\to V_h$ for which there is a constant $C_F$ such that
$$\|\Pi_hv\|_V\le C_F\|v\|_V\quad(v\in V),\qquad b(\Pi_hv,q_h)=b(v,q_h)\quad(v\in V,\ q_h\in Q_h).$$
The second condition is exact constraint preservation. It does not assert $\operatorname{div}\Pi_hv=\operatorname{div}v$ pointwise.
lem-na-fortin-transfers-discrete-infsup:
## Statement

Let $V_h\subset V$ and $Q_h\subset Q$, and suppose the continuous inf-sup constant of $b$ is $\beta>0$. If $Q_h=\{0\}$ the constraint assertion is vacuous. Otherwise, for a Fortin operator as in [[def-na-fortin-operator]] with bound $C_F$, define $\beta_h:=\inf_{q_h\ne0}\sup_{v_h\ne0}b(v_h,q_h)/(\|v_h\|_V\|q_h\|_Q)$. Then $\beta_h\ge\beta/C_F$.
thm-na-babuska-brezzi-kernel-coercivity:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V,Q$ be real Hilbert spaces, and let $a:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ and $b:V\times Q\to\mathbb R$ be bounded bilinear forms. If $Q=\{0\}$, the theorem reduces to Lax–Milgram on $V$ with $Z=V$ and $p=0$. Otherwise, if $Q\ne\{0\}$, assume $V\ne\{0\}$. Define $B:V\to Q$ by $(Bv,q)_Q=b(v,q)$ and set $\beta:=\inf_{q\ne0}\sup_{v\ne0}b(v,q)/(\|v\|_V\|q\|_Q)>0$. Suppose $Z:=\ker B$ is closed and $a(z,z)\ge\alpha\|z\|_V^2$ on $Z$, with $\alpha>0$. For every $F\in V'$ and $G\in Q'$, there is a unique $(u,p)\in V\times Q$ satisfying
$$a(u,v)+b(v,p)=F(v),\qquad b(u,q)=G(q),$$
for all $v\in V,q\in Q$. If $M_a=\|a\|$, then one stability bound is
$$\|u\|_V\le\beta^{-1}\|G\|+\alpha^{-1}(\|F\|+M_a\beta^{-1}\|G\|),\qquad \|p\|_Q\le\beta^{-1}(\|F\|+M_a\|u\|_V).$$
thm-na-mixed-galerkin-quasioptimality:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V,Q$ be real Hilbert spaces and let $F\in V\prime$, $G\in Q\prime$ be bounded data. Suppose bounded bilinear forms $a,b$ and $(u,p)\in V\times Q$ satisfy
$$a(u,v)+b(v,p)=F(v),\qquad b(u,q)=G(q)$$
for all $v\in V,q\in Q$. Let $V_h\subset V$, $Q_h\subset Q$ be finite-dimensional conforming subspaces, with $Q_h\ne\{0\}$ and discrete inf-sup constant $\beta_h:=\inf_{q_h\ne0}\sup_{v_h\ne0}b(v_h,q_h)/(\|v_h\|_V\|q_h\|_Q)>0$. Assume the **discrete** kernel coercivity $a(v_h,v_h)\ge\alpha_*\|v_h\|_V^2$ for every $v_h\in Z_h:=\{w_h:b(w_h,q_h)=0\text{ for all }q_h\in Q_h\}$, where $\alpha_*>0$. Put $M_a=\|a\|$, $M_b=\|b\|$. The Galerkin system with the same $F,G$ has a unique solution $(u_h,p_h)$. For any $w_h\in V_h$, $r_h\in Q_h$, define $\delta_u=\|u-w_h\|_V$, $\delta_p=\|p-r_h\|_Q$, $R_h=\beta_h^{-1}M_b\delta_u$, and
$$U_h=\delta_u+\alpha_*^{-1}\{M_a(\delta_u+R_h)+M_b\delta_p\}+R_h,$$
$$P_h=\delta_p+\beta_h^{-1}\{M_a(U_h+\delta_u)+M_b\delta_p\}.$$
Then $\|u-u_h\|_V\le U_h$ and $\|p-p_h\|_Q\le P_h$. In particular the pressure bound retains $\beta_h^{-1}$ explicitly; taking infima over $w_h,r_h$ gives the corresponding best-approximation bound.
lem-na-scott-zhang-boundary-preserving-p:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain with a conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh, $d=2$ or $3$, mesh size $h=\max_Kh_K$. For each interior mesh vertex $z$, choose any incident facet $F_z$; for each boundary vertex choose an incident boundary facet. Let $\psi_{z,F_z}\in P_1(F_z)$ be the unique dual affine function satisfying $\int_{F_z}\psi_{z,F_z}\varphi_y=\delta_{zy}$ for the facet's P1 nodal basis. Define
$$I_hv=\sum_z\left(\int_{F_z}\psi_{z,F_z}\operatorname{tr}v\right)\varphi_z.$$
This is a linear face-average interpolant $H^1(D)\to S_h$, where $S_h$ is the continuous piecewise P1 space. It maps $H^1_0(D)$ into $S_h\cap H^1_0(D)$, is uniformly $H^1$-seminorm stable, and for each element patch $\omega_K$ has
$$\|v-I_hv\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}.$$
If $v\in H^2(D)$, then $\|\nabla(v-I_hv)\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch_K\|D^2v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. Constants depend only on dimension, the fixed domain, and the mesh shape-regularity bound. No point evaluation is used.
def-na-mini-element-p1-bubble-p1-spaces:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d=2$ or $3$, be a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain with a conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$. On a simplex $K$ with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$, define the scalar interior bubble $b_K=(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{i=0}^d\lambda_i$. Let
$$S^1_h=\{w\in C^0(\overline D):w|_K\in P_1(K)\},\quad S^1_{h,0}=S^1_h\cap H^1_0(D).$$
The **mini-element spaces** are
$$V_h=[S^1_{h,0}]^d\oplus\bigoplus_{K\in\mathcal T_h}b_K\mathbb R^d\subset H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d),\qquad Q_h=S^1_h\cap L^2_0(D).$$
Each bubble is extended by zero off its cell. The zero-boundary conformity of the piecewise affine part is supplied by [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]. The local/global dimensions are proved in the next dimension lemma.
lem-na-mini-element-local-and-global-dim:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For a connected conforming simplicial mesh in dimension $d=2$ or $3$, the local scalar velocity polynomial space $P_1(K)\oplus\operatorname{span}\{b_K\}$ has dimension $d+2$, the vector velocity dimension is $d(d+2)$, and the local pressure space $P_1(K)$ has dimension $d+1$. If the mesh has $N_v$ vertices, $N_{v,0}$ interior vertices and $N_K$ cells, then
$$\dim V_h=dN_{v,0}+dN_K,\qquad \dim Q_h=N_v-1.$$
thm-na-mini-element-fortin-stability:
## Statement

On the mini-element spaces of [[def-na-mini-element-p1-bubble-p1-spaces]], there is a Fortin operator $\Pi_h:V\to V_h$ preserving $b(v,q_h)$ for every $q_h\in Q_h$, with $\|\Pi_hv\|_V\le C_F\|v\|_V$. The constant depends only on $d$ and the mesh shape-regularity bound, not on $h$. Consequently
$$\beta_h\ge (C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-1}.$$
def-na-discrete-weak-and-exact-divergenc:
## Definition

For the conforming mini-element spaces $V_h,Q_h$, define the **weak discrete divergence kernel** by
$$Z_h:=\{v_h\in V_h:b(v_h,q_h)=0\text{ for every }q_h\in Q_h\},$$
and the **exact discrete divergence kernel** by
$$Z_h^0:=\{v_h\in V_h:\operatorname{div}v_h=0\text{ almost everywhere on }D\}.$$
Since $b(v_h,q_h)=-\int_Dq_h\operatorname{div}v_h$, one has $Z_h^0\subseteq Z_h$. Equality is not part of either definition; the companion example proves strictness for a concrete mesh.
thm-na-mini-element-h1-pressure-error:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain in dimension $d=2$ or $3$, with a conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh family of mesh size $h$. Put $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$. For $\nu>0$ and $F\in V'$, suppose $(u,p)\in V\times Q$ satisfies
$$2\nu\int_D\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)-\int_Dp\,\operatorname{div}v=F(v),\qquad -\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}u=0$$
for every $v\in V,q\in Q$, with $u\in H^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $p\in H^1(D)$. Let $(u_h,p_h)\in V_h\times Q_h$ solve the same equations for every $v_h\in V_h,q_h\in Q_h$, where $V_h,Q_h$ are the P1-bubble/P1 mini spaces. Then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{H^1(D)}+\|p-p_h\|_{L^2(D)}\le C h(\|u\|_{H^2(D)}+\|p\|_{H^1(D)}).$$
The constant is independent of $h$ and depends on $d$, $D$, shape regularity, $\nu$, $C_{\rm div}(D)$, and the Poincare constant. The mixed error formula retains $M_a=2\nu$, $M_b=\sqrt d$, discrete-kernel coercivity $\alpha_*=\nu$, and $\beta_h\ge(C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-1}$ explicitly.
thm-na-discrete-helmholtz-projection-and:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V_h,Q_h$ be the stable mini-element spaces on a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain with a conforming mesh, with viscosity $\nu>0$, and let $Z_h=\{v_h:b(v_h,q_h)=0\ \forall q_h\in Q_h\}$. Choose bases of $V_h,Q_h$, let $M$ be the velocity mass matrix, $A$ the Stokes stiffness matrix, and $B$ the constraint matrix with entries $B_{\ell j}=b(\phi_j,\chi_\ell)$. The mass-orthogonal projector onto $Z_h$ is
$$P_M=I-M^{-1}B^T(BM^{-1}B^T)^{-1}B.$$
On the mean-zero pressure coordinates, both the mass pressure Schur matrix $BM^{-1}B^T$ and stiffness pressure Schur matrix $BA^{-1}B^T$ are positive definite. Before imposing the pressure gauge on the full continuous P1 space, the constant pressure is exactly the one-dimensional nullspace of $B^T$.
thm-na-weak-stokes-solvability-lipschitz:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected and Lipschitz, $d=2$ or $3$, and let $\nu>0$. For every bounded linear functional $F$ on $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ equipped with $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_2$, there is a unique $(u,p)\in V\times Q$, $Q=L^2_0(D)$, satisfying
$$2\nu\int_D\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)-\int_Dp\operatorname{div}v=F(v),\qquad -\int_Dq\operatorname{div}u=0$$
for every $v\in V,q\in Q$. The pressure is normalized to have mean zero. One stability bound is $\|u\|_V\le\nu^{-1}\|F\|_{V'}$ and $\|p\|_2\le3C_{\rm div}(D)\|F\|_{V'}$.
ex-na-mini-element-bubble-moment:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a $d$-simplex, $b_K>0$ its interior barycentric bubble, and $q\in P_1(K)$ a nonconstant affine pressure. Define the local pairing $b_K(v,q):=-\int_Kq\,\operatorname{div}v$ and let $v=b_K\nabla q$. Then $b_K(v,q)=\int_Kb_K|\nabla q|^2>0$. This positive cell contribution does not by itself prove a global inf-sup bound.
ex-na-taylor-hood-pressure-mode:
## Statement

On the reference right triangle $K=\{(x,y):x\ge0,y\ge0,x+y\le1\}$, let $q(x,y)=x-1/3$ and $v(x,y)=(x^2,0)$. Then $q$ has zero cell mean and the local Stokes pairing is $-\int_Kq\operatorname{div}v=-1/18$. This is a local mode-detection calculation only; it proves no global Taylor–Hood stability theorem.
ex-na-weakly-versus-exactly-divergence-f:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. On a square split into two triangles, the mini-element weak divergence kernel contains a nonzero velocity whose divergence is not zero almost everywhere. Thus the weak discrete kernel $Z_h$ can strictly contain the exact kernel $Z_h^0$.
